From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call recap + quantified economics & flightplan

Maria — thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap from my side and a suggested flightplan so we can get you a scoped pilot that matches BlueBridge's budget and ROI timeline.

Key pain points you called out:
- Production inference spend increasing unpredictably as feature usage scales (current estimate: $30k/month on existing provider).
- 99th percentile latencies occasionally spike above 600ms causing timeouts in the checkout flow.
- Procurement needs a clear, line-item TCO comparison and a 6-month ROI case to move to pilot.

Goals we agreed on:
- Prototype the new recommendation endpoint with latency target: p95 < 250ms, p99 < 400ms.
- Keep pilot budget under $20k/month (including egress and storage) while proving a 30% unit-cost reduction vs current baseline.
- Demonstrate user-facing latency improvements and no regression in prediction quality (A/B).

Observed levers and recommended initial stack:
1) Batching & adaptive routing — set conservative batching windows for background traffic and low-latency lanes for checkout.
2) Prefix/KV caching — cache frequent user prefixes (cart-level prompts) to cut token counts by ~18-25% on repeat flows.
3) Quantization & smaller model variant for lower-cost paths — use int8/4 quantized llama-style variant for background scoring.
4) Dedicated pool during peak hours to guarantee latency SLOs; fallback to hosted cheaper variants off-peak.

Attached: redwood-token-econ-worksheet.xlsx with quick TCO slices (per-token, per-call, queueing overhead), and a 1-page pilot scope (bluebridge-pilot-scope.pdf). I also included a short security checklist to share with your procurement team.

Next steps (proposed):
- I’ll send a tightened pilot budget and a side-by-side TCO (hosted vs dedicated) by EOD Monday. ACTION: Jordan to deliver TCO worksheet update.
- Schedule a 30-min technical sync with your infra/security + our solutions engineer to validate the caching surface and data-flow (target Tues 21 Jul). ACTION: Maria to confirm availability and security attendees.
- If procurement agrees to the budget envelope, we’ll ship a two-week pilot with success metrics: cost/unit delta, p95/p99 latency, and quality delta (Δ top-1 accuracy).

If this aligns, I’ll open the HubSpot deal and add a mutual action plan visible to both teams.

Thanks,
Jordan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
